text:
[RFCS.16.2] A field number's **band** fixes the forward-compat disposition a reader
with **no table entry** for that number must apply — this is the entire number-encoded
adjudication surface, exactly **three** dispositions:

| Band | Range | Unknown-number disposition |
|---|---|---|
| inject | `1–127` | **reject** → `DS_ERR_FS_UNKNOWN_INJECT` |
| reject-don't-skip | `128–255` | **reject** → `DS_ERR_DSC_VERSION` |
| skip-don't-reject | `256–2047` | **skip** (log info) |

The boundaries are powers of two (128, 256, 2048) so band classification is a high-bit
test. `1–15` are simply the inject slots that carry a **1-byte** protobuf tag (field
numbers < 16); `16–2047` are 2-byte (2047 is the max 2-byte field number — 2048 tips to
3). Skip-don't-reject is the large, growing band (all of `256–2047`); inject and
reject-don't-skip stay small and bounded.

cbmc.name: rfcs_16_2__band_is_total
cbmc.note: UNBOUNDED over all 2^32 field numbers. Proves the SHAPE — the bands are total, disjoint and exhaustive — not the VALUES: it states the partition in the same constants the implementation uses, so a shifted boundary is still a partition. Seeding DS_ATOM_BAND_REJECT_HI 255->254 left this green.

cbmc.name: rfcs_16_2__boundaries_are_exact
cbmc.note: UNBOUNDED. Pins the VALUES with literals — 0/1/127/128/255/256/2047/2048 and the 1-byte sub-range of [RFCS.16.4]. This is the harness that caught the seeded 255->254 off-by-one, on the one assertion that names that boundary.

cbmc.name: rfcs_16_3__unknown_is_decided_by_band_alone
cbmc.note: BOUNDED, --unwind 9, and the bound is DERIVED not chosen: ds_pbf_lookup's binary search over DS_ATOM_REGISTRY_COUNT terminates in at most ceil(log2(N))+1 iterations, which for any N <= 255 is at most 8. The bound is slack. Run with --unwinding-assertions, and that assertion PASSED — so CBMC proved the bound sufficient rather than assuming it. The bound must rise if the registry exceeds 255 entries; the unwinding assertion is what will catch that.
